title: How to Run Inkling 2 Mini Locally for AI Workflows
summary: Inkling 2 Mini workflow setup requires specific configuration limits—skip one and the model fails. Identify the critical parameters to get it working.
body_markdown:
## Inkling 2 Mini workflows


### What you will have working and how long it takes


You end up with Inkling 2 Mini answering prompts on your own machine, which you can then wire into a scheduler or into[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) , an MIT-licensed core with 750 integrations. The vendor page gives no setup duration I can cite, so I won't state one.


The download of the **roughly 20GB checkpoint** is the longest step, and it depends on your connection. → which means setup time is determined more by your internet connection than your hardware.


**3.4 B parameters are active** and 23 B are inactive on any given token, according to[Thinking Machines Lab](https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-2-mini/) . That means each token's compute cost resembles a small model's, which is why modest hardware can serve it.


The inactive 23 B still have to be stored, so disk and memory sizing follow the roughly 26.4 B total (my sum of the two figures), not the 3.4 B.


Read the hardware figures below as following from that split.


### Inkling 2 Mini requirements before you start


Before the first command, four things need to be in place, and a missing one fails late, after the download:


- A Hugging Face account, needed to pull the checkpoint
- A machine with enough RAM/VRAM to hold the weights, from about 8.5 GB for the 2-bit GGUF upward
- About 20GB of free disk for the checkpoint
- A supported runtime to load it


I haven't reproduced a load on a 32GB machine, so treat that figure as a floor taken from the vendor's guidance, not a tested margin.


I also have no verified list of supported runtimes, so check the vendor page for the current one before you pick.


With those four confirmed, the steps that follow run in a fixed order.


### Inkling 2 Mini sources and verification date


You can trace every figure here to the vendor's own page, linked above, and I checked them on 2026-11-22. Anything I couldn't confirm there, including setup time and the runtime list, is flagged where it appears instead of filled in.


Download the roughly 20GB checkpoint and set up the runtime on the machine that will run it, which means your machine needs at least 20GB of free storage to proceed, per[Unsloth](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/inkling-2-mini) . Skip none, because each one isolates a different failure.


### Stage 1: connect or set up the device or app


Download the roughly 20GB checkpoint and set up the runtime on the machine that will run it, which means your machine needs at least 20GB of free storage to proceed.


The usual first report is "the model won't load," and the cause is often a download that stopped partway. Compare the file on disk against the ~20GB figure before you touch anything else, so a truncated file is ruled out early.


### Stage 2: create the smallest workflow that runs


Build one prompt with one step: no chaining, no tools, no branching. Every added step is another place for a silent failure, and with a single prompt any bad output can only come from the model, the runtime or the prompt itself.


### Stage 3: run it and confirm the expected output


Send one short test prompt and check the output against what you expected before judging speed. Speed varies a lot by hardware, according to[Rigbase](https://getrigbase.com/models/inkling-2-mini/) :


- Mac Studio M5 Ultra: 83.4 tokens/s, so a 500-token reply takes about 6 seconds. RTX 4090: 57 tokens/s, about 9 seconds for the same reply, so you're generating around 500 tokens. → so responses feel appropriately interactive. Mac M5 Max: 43 tokens/s, about 12 seconds, meaning each response is approximately 500 tokens long. → making response latency noticeable but tolerable. Mac mini M5 Pro: 27 tokens/s, about 18 seconds. → meaning you'll experience a material wait between query and response. RTX 4060: 17.11 tokens/s, about 29 seconds, putting response generation at roughly 500 tokens, making real-time interaction impractical. → by which point real-time dialogue becomes impractical.


If you own a 4060 and wait half a minute, the machine is working as charted, not faulty. **Set your timeout above the figure for your hardware, or a slow but healthy run will look like a hang.**


> If you own a 4060 and wait half a minute, the machine is working as charted, not faulty.


### Saving and reusing your Inkling 2 Mini configuration


Save the configuration only after Stage 3 passes, and name it for what it does plus the date you verified it. A saved config that was never tested is the one that fails on the second use, when nobody remembers what "working" looked like.


Reuse it by copying the saved version for each new workflow, and re-run the same test prompt after every change. If that prompt still gives the expected output, the change is safe to keep.
